# Check reference

<!-- Written by npm run docs:gen. Do not edit this file: change a script's .meta.ts beside it in packages/harness/src/, or the code, and run npm run docs:gen. npm run check:docs fails when this file is stale. -->

Every script the harness runs: what it is for, what it reads and what it fails. Each script's meta, `packages/harness/src/<script>.meta.ts`, gives the words. The rest is read from the code: the script names and the build gate from `package.json`, the rule checks from `check:rules`, the flags each script accepts, whether it compares with the base or opens Chrome from the code it runs, and the fixture cases from each `case.ts` under `packages/harness/fixtures/`.

## The build gate

```sh
npm run check:fixtures && npm run check
```

`npm run check` runs `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `check:products`, `check:proposals`, `check:retirement`, `check:loop` and `check:docs`, in that order, and stops at the first failure. `check:products` runs `check:product` on every product's config, which runs `check:opt-outs`, `lint:product-ui`, `lint:slots`, `check:step-budget`, `check:disclosure`, `check:priority`, `check:one-thing`, `check:inventories`, `check:state-coverage`, `check:target-size`, `check:accessible-names` and `check:rendered-page`, in that order, and skips a rule the config opts out of.

**Base.** `check:inventories`, `check:proposals`, `check:retirement` and `check:trace` compare the change with its base. The base is `INVENTORY_BASE` when it is set: CI sets it to the pull request base, or on a push to `main` to `github.event.before`, the tip of `main` before the push. A base missing from the clone fails the check. Unset, empty, `true`, `false` or all zeros, it is the merge base with `origin/main`, or with a local `main`. Without either, the check fails.

**Chrome.** `check:target-size`, `check:accessible-names`, `check:rendered-page`, `check:products`, `check:product` and `screenshots` need headless Chrome, because they open pages in it or run a check that does, and so do the fixture cases that run a Chrome check without `--list`. They find Chrome at `CHROME_PATH`, then the chrome-headless-shell build that `puppeteer-core` pins, which `npm run setup:chrome` installs into `.cache/chrome` (CI runs the same script), then the usual `/usr/bin` paths. A `CHROME_PATH` that names no file fails on its own. With no Chrome, the check fails, naming each place it looked and both fixes.

## `lint:product-ui`

Product UI is built only from the product's catalog: no raw controls, no inline styles, no other component kit, nothing from another product.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run lint:product-ui`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/lint-product-ui.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it.

It fails:

- A design system import anywhere but the catalog, an import from one of the foreign component kits the check lists, or a relative import that reaches outside the product's own directories, such as into another product.
- A raw `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea` or `a` element anywhere in product UI, the catalog included, or a `style` attribute outside the catalog.
- Any of those imports in any form: re-exports (`export ... from`), `import()`, `require()` (also as `globalThis.require` or `(0, require)`), `import x = require()` and Vite's `import.meta.glob` all count.
- A dynamic load whose specifier is not a string literal, because it cannot be checked, and `require` held under another name.

It reads the product's UI roots from the config: `paths.features`, `paths.pageTypes`, `paths.layouts`, `paths.contentLayouts`, `paths.app` and the catalog's own folder. The adapter's own packages are not foreign. A loader made with `createRequire` is not read. A product cannot opt out of this rule.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `catalog-loads`: Legal: re-exports and dynamic imports of the product's own catalog pass the off-catalog lint. It passes with "off-catalog: clean".
- `fake-ds`: Legal under the stand-in adapter, which shares no name with Todae. Run on the Todae adapter, every check here but the off-catalog lint fails these pages, so passing shows a check reads its names from the adapter. It passes with "off-catalog: clean".
- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "off-catalog: clean".
- `illegal/dynamic-design-system-import`: Illegal: `import()` of the design system outside the catalog, and an `import()` the lint cannot read. It fails with "off-catalog: import "@tounsoo/todae" directly" and fails with "with a computed specifier cannot be checked".
- `illegal/fake-ds-off-catalog`: Illegal under the stand-in adapter: its package imported outside the catalog. It fails with "off-catalog: import "@fake/ds" directly".
- `illegal/indirect-require`: Illegal: `globalThis.require(...)`, `(0, require)(...)` and `require` held under another name load the design system outside the catalog. It fails with "off-catalog: import "@tounsoo/todae" directly", fails with "off-catalog: import "@tounsoo/todae/styles.css" directly" and fails with "require is held under another name".
- `illegal/off-catalog`: Illegal: raw controls and a direct design system import outside the catalog. It fails with "raw <button> is not a catalog control".
- `illegal/other-product-catalog`: Illegal: a page imports another product's catalog by a relative path, so it reaches parts its own catalog does not export. It fails with "reaches outside this product's directories".
- `illegal/re-exported-design-system`: Illegal: an `export ... from` of the design system outside the catalog. It fails with "off-catalog: import "@tounsoo/todae" directly".

## `lint:slots`

Each page type with a primary slot holds its page's one primary action there.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run lint:slots`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-slots.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it.

It fails:

- A page whose primary slot is missing, as when the shell is self-closed (`<Shell />`), or that renders the slot more than once; a slot that does not hold exactly one action control, or holds one that is not primary.
- A slot name the page type's shell does not define as `Object.assign(Root, { ... })`, in its module or a module it re-exports from, so a misspelled slot fails instead of matching nothing.
- A page type named there that renders no page, or that is not in `allowed_page_types`, and a config that names no page type, so the rule cannot go quiet. A page type in none or more than one of `shells.primarySlots`, `shells.collections` and `shells.content` fails here too.
- A page type in `allowed_page_types` with no shell module under `paths.pageTypes`, or whose module exports no shell.

The check does not name `DetailPage`: `shells.primarySlots` maps a page type to its slot, Meridian's `{ detail: "Primary" }`, and the shell's name comes from that page type's module. A second primary outside the slot is `check:priority`'s to catch.

A variant computed from an expression, such as `variant={tone}`, counts as neither primary nor secondary, so one in the slot fails here and in `check:priority`.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `content-page`: Legal: a third kind of page, help, which the config names under shells.content. It shows information and holds no primary action, so it is neither a primary-slot page nor a collection. It passes with "exactly one primary button on 1 detail page".
- `fake-ds`: Legal under the stand-in adapter, which shares no name with Todae. Run on the Todae adapter, every check here but the off-catalog lint fails these pages, so passing shows a check reads its names from the adapter. It passes with "exactly one primary button on 1 detail page".
- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "exactly one primary button on 1 detail page".
- `shell-imported-then-exported`: Legal: the detail page type's index.ts imports its shell and then exports it. The slot names are read through that import. It passes with "exactly one primary button on 1 detail page".
- `two-detail-pages`: Legal: two detail pages, each with one primary Approve. Priority holds per page, so a product may render the rank-1 action on as many pages as it needs. It passes with "exactly one primary button on 2 detail page".
- `illegal/fake-ds-two-primaries`: Illegal under the stand-in adapter: two strong actions in the primary slot. It fails with "found 2 primary and 2 Action".
- `illegal/misspelled-primary-slot`: Illegal: the config names the detail shell's primary slot "Primry". DetailPage has no such slot. It fails with "names slot "Primry" for page type "detail", but DetailPage has no such slot".
- `illegal/no-primary-slot`: Illegal: no page type has a primary slot, so lint:slots would check nothing. It fails with "shells.primarySlots names no page type, so no primary slot is checked".
- `illegal/page-type-in-both-rules`: Illegal: the config names detail as a primary-slot page and a collection, which ask for one primary action and none. It fails with "page type "detail" in both primarySlots and collections".
- `illegal/page-type-in-primary-and-content`: Illegal: the config names detail as a primary-slot page and a content page, which ask for one primary action and none. It fails with "page type "detail" in both primarySlots and content, but a content page has no primary action".
- `illegal/primary-slot-from-config`: Illegal: the config names the detail shell's Secondary slot as its primary slot, so lint:slots reads that slot and finds no primary action in it. It fails with "accepts exactly one primary button, found 0 primary and 1 Button.Root".
- `illegal/shell-rule-unknown-page-type`: Illegal: the shells rules name page types the product does not allow, so a rule would have no shell to read. It fails with "shells.primarySlots names page type "form", which is not in allowed_page_types".
- `illegal/two-primaries`: Illegal: two buttons in the detail page's primary slot. It fails with "accepts exactly one primary button, found 2 primary".
- `illegal/unclassified-page-type`: Illegal: the config names no collection, though the product has a collection page type, so the collection rules would read none of its pages. It fails with "page type "collection" in neither primarySlots nor collections".

## `check:step-budget`

Every route that finishes a task, not only the shortest, fits that task's `max_steps`, in the task graph and in the shipped reducer.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run check:step-budget`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-step-budget.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it.

It fails:

- A task in the inputs' `tasks` with no task graph mapped under `flows[].tasks`, a mapped id that is not a task, a task mapped to two graphs, a graph file that is missing, or a graph whose `taskId` is not the id it is mapped under.
- A graph module that does not export `flowStart`, `userEvents` and `transition`, so the shipped flow cannot be measured, or that exports a `flowStatus` that is not a function.
- A modeled path (the task graph's shortest) or shipped path (the flow's `transition` reducer's shortest, from `flowStart` over `userEvents` to the task's `success_state`) that is missing or longer than `max_steps`.
- A modeled path and shipped path that are not the same steps.
- Any longer route to the same success over `max_steps`, in the graph or the reducer.
- A reached flow state with no name: neither a `status` field nor a `flowStatus(state)` exported by the graph module.
- A task whose search would measure more than 10,000 states, or look at more than 200,000 states for the shortest finishes.

A step is an event that a task graph in the same `flows[]` entry names, so with a hold-room task beside book-room, hold then book is a route to booked. A route takes any steps the flow allows, each at most once and never back to a state it has passed, then finishes the shortest way any user event allows. Events no task names, such as an optional look or Back, count only when the finish needs them. The search stops a route once it passes the budget, and measures a state once when no earlier state on the route can come back after it, so steps that can come in any order do not multiply. Two states are the same when they hold the same values, whatever order their keys were written in, and a Set or Map is read by what it holds. `measureRoutes` in `lib/shortest-path.ts` does the search.

Steps that are not events, such as scrolling, reading or opening a disclosure to find something, cost nothing here. When the shortest path has two candidates, `shortestPath` returns the first in edge order, so order the edges or `userEvents` so the reviewed one comes first.

For each task it prints `longest shipped flow route (N)` beside its verdict; quote that line when a change touches a reducer, a task graph or a budget.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `flow-status`: Legal: a flow whose states keep their name in phase, read through the graph module's flowStatus. It passes with "step budget: within budget.".
- `longer-route`: Legal: a second, longer route to a task's success that fits its budget, measured and printed. It passes with "longest shipped flow route (3): open-note → send-reminder → archive".
- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "step budget: within budget.".
- `two-tasks`: Legal: a notes inbox with two tasks, each mapped to its own task graph, and a preview query for one modeled state only. It passes with "step budget: archive-note (max_steps 2)".
- `illegal/flow-state-without-status`: Illegal: a flow whose states have no status field and a graph module with no flowStatus. It fails with "which has no status field".
- `illegal/graph-flow-drift`: Illegal: a 3-step task graph whose shipped reducer needs 2 steps. It fails with "does not match the modeled path".
- `illegal/graph-without-task-id`: Illegal: the two-task product with archive-note mapped to a graph that exports no taskId, so the mapping alone says which task it models. It fails with "does not export a taskId".
- `illegal/modeled-route-over-budget`: Illegal: a 2-step shortest path, and a 4-step modeled route to the same success, for a task with max_steps 3. It fails with "the modeled route open-invoice → flag → add-note → approve takes 4 steps, which exceeds max_steps 3".
- `illegal/over-budget`: Illegal: a task graph that needs 4 steps for a task with max_steps 3. It fails with "modeled path length 4 exceeds max_steps".
- `illegal/over-budget-flow`: Illegal: a 3-step task graph whose shipped reducer needs 4 steps. It fails with "shipped flow path length 4 exceeds max_steps".
- `illegal/route-over-budget`: Illegal: archive-note's shortest path, open then archive, fits max_steps 2, but the reducer also lets a reminded note be archived. That route is 3 steps. It fails with "the shipped flow route open-note → send-reminder → archive takes 3 steps, which exceeds max_steps 2 for archive-note".
- `illegal/second-task-over-budget`: Illegal: the two-task product with its second task over budget. It fails with "modeled path length 3 exceeds max_steps 2 for archive-note".
- `illegal/task-without-graph`: Illegal: the two-task product with a task graph for only one of its two tasks. It fails with "task "archive-note" has no task graph".

## `check:disclosure`

Each page holds at most `MAX_DISCLOSURES_PER_PAGE` disclosures, nested at most `MAX_DISCLOSURE_DEPTH` deep.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run check:disclosure`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-disclosure.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it.

It fails:

- A page with more `Disclosure.Root` elements than `MAX_DISCLOSURES_PER_PAGE`, counted across every component the page renders.
- Disclosures nested deeper than `MAX_DISCLOSURE_DEPTH`, followed across components.
- A disclosure in the features path that no page reaches, such as JSX held in a variable outside the shell, because a per-page cap cannot count it.
- No page found, or a catalog that stops exporting the adapter's disclosure.

A page is one rendered page-type shell in the config's `paths.features`, plus what renders on it: components its JSX uses (local, or imported from a relative path), its content layouts, the page-type shell module, and the chrome layouts. `lib/page-scope.ts` builds that scope, and `check:priority` and `check:one-thing` use the same one. It follows JSX tags and calls to helper functions, undoes import aliases such as `Field as F`, and follows a component imported under another name, a default export, and a named export through a barrel's `export { X } from` or `export *`.

The caps come from the product's `rules` module. It does not read whether a disclosure starts open, or what sits outside disclosures.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `fake-ds`: Legal under the stand-in adapter, which shares no name with Todae. Run on the Todae adapter, every check here but the off-catalog lint fails these pages, so passing shows a check reads its names from the adapter. It passes with "across 2 pages".
- `imported-page-parts`: Legal: the page's actions and disclosure come in under an alias, as a default export, and through an `export *` barrel. The page scope follows each, so priority sees them on the page. It passes with "at most 1 per page, across 1 pages".
- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "across 2 pages".
- `illegal/disclosures-per-page`: Illegal: one disclosure in each of two component files on one page. It fails with "more than 1 per page".
- `illegal/fake-ds-hoisted`: Illegal under the stand-in adapter: a disclosure and a question held outside any page. It fails with "Reveal.Root is not reached from any page".
- `illegal/fake-ds-nested-reveal`: Illegal under the stand-in adapter: a disclosure inside a disclosure. It fails with "disclosure depth 2 exceeds 1".
- `illegal/fake-ds-over-caps`: Illegal under the stand-in adapter: two disclosures, two questions in the open, and the strong action inside a disclosure. It fails with "page has 2 disclosures".

## `check:priority`

Each page holds at most one primary action, and it is the product's rank-1 action; the rank-2 action is secondary; `disclosed_sections` stay behind disclosures.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run check:priority`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-priority.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it.

It fails:

- On a page: more than one primary button, a primary whose text is not the rank-1 action in `priority` (Meridian's Approve), or a primary inside a disclosure, including one in a component the page renders.
- On a page: the rank-2 action (Meridian's Request changes) shown as primary or more than once.
- On any page: an action button whose variant is computed, such as `variant={tone}`, because it could be a second primary.
- Across the product: no page with the rank-1 primary, or a rank-1 or rank-2 button no page reaches.
- A section in `disclosed_sections` that is not the text of a `Disclosure.Summary`.

The rules hold per page, in the page scope `check:disclosure` describes, with import aliases undone and `UI.Button.Root` through `import * as UI` read too. A product may render as many pages as it needs, so two record pages may each hold the rank-1 action. Actions are matched by their button text, so a translation breaks the match.

Write a button's variant as a plain string, as in `variant="secondary"`. A braced literal, `variant={"secondary"}`, is read as the variant too, but also as part of the button's text, so "Request changes" becomes "secondary Request changes" and the check fails. A button with no variant is primary, because the adapter says Todae's default is.

Two shapes are not seen: a button passed as children into a component that wraps its children in a disclosure, and a tag held in a local variable, such as `const Control = Button`. The sections in `disclosed_sections` come from the product's inputs, not from the script.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `fake-ds`: Legal under the stand-in adapter, which shares no name with Todae. Run on the Todae adapter, every check here but the off-catalog lint fails these pages, so passing shows a check reads its names from the adapter. It passes with ""Approve" is the primary button".
- `imported-page-parts`: Legal: the page's actions and disclosure come in under an alias, as a default export, and through an `export *` barrel. The page scope follows each, so priority sees them on the page. It passes with ""Approve" is the primary button on 1 of 1 pages".
- `own-sections`: Legal: inputs that disclose "Attachments", and pages that put it behind a disclosure. It passes with "disclosed: "Attachments"".
- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with ""Approve" is the primary button".
- `two-detail-pages`: Legal: two detail pages, each with one primary Approve. Priority holds per page, so a product may render the rank-1 action on as many pages as it needs. It passes with ""Approve" is the primary button on 2 of 2 pages".
- `illegal/aliased-second-primary`: Illegal: two primary buttons on one page, one of them imported under another name. It fails with "page has 2 primary buttons".
- `illegal/computed-variant`: Illegal: a button whose variant is computed. The check cannot tell whether it is a second primary, so it fails it. It fails with "has a computed variant, so the check cannot tell whether it is primary".
- `illegal/fake-ds-over-caps`: Illegal under the stand-in adapter: two disclosures, two questions in the open, and the strong action inside a disclosure. It fails with "a primary button is inside a disclosure".
- `illegal/missing-disclosed-section`: Illegal: line items shown in the open. It fails with "is not behind a disclosure".
- `illegal/namespace-second-primary`: Illegal: two primary buttons on one page, one of them written as `UI.Button.Root` through `import * as UI`. It fails with "page has 2 primary buttons".
- `illegal/page-inside-disclosure`: Illegal: a disclosure around the page shell hides its primary action. It fails with "a primary button is inside a disclosure".
- `illegal/primary-in-imported-disclosure`: Illegal: a primary button inside a disclosure, where the button and the disclosure are in different files. It fails with "a primary button is inside a disclosure".
- `illegal/renamed-disclosed-section`: Illegal: the own-sections inputs, which disclose "Attachments", on the fixture product's pages, which disclose only Line items. It fails with ""Attachments" is not behind a disclosure".

## `check:one-thing`

One job per page: no page inside a page, no primary on a collection or content page, and at most `MAX_VISIBLE_QUESTIONS` questions outside a disclosure.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run check:one-thing`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-one-thing.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it.

It fails:

- A page rendered inside another page, in its own JSX or through a component it renders, including one imported under another name.
- A page type in `allowed_page_types` that renders no page.
- A primary button on a collection page, including inside a content layout that page uses.
- A primary button on a content page, one whose page type is under `shells.content`, anywhere it reaches but the chrome layouts every page shares, and a button there whose variant is computed, so the check cannot tell it is not primary.
- More questions outside a disclosure on one page than `MAX_VISIBLE_QUESTIONS`. A question is the adapter's question part, Todae's `Field.Root`.
- A chrome slot in `shells.collections` that the collection's shell does not define, or that it names for a shell not defined as `Object.assign(Root, { ... })`; a page type there that is not in `allowed_page_types`; and an allowed page type named in none or more than one of `shells.primarySlots`, `shells.collections` and `shells.content`, or a page type under `shells.content` that is not in `allowed_page_types`.
- A page type in `allowed_page_types` with no shell module under `paths.pageTypes`, or whose module exports no shell.
- A catalog that stops exporting the question part, so the cap cannot go quiet.

A page type is one of three kinds in the config's `shells`: `primarySlots`, one primary action in a named slot; `collections`, no primary and a registered content layout in the body; or the optional `content`, a page that shows information, such as a help or policy page, and holds no primary button outside the shared chrome layouts.

`allowed_page_types` decides which shells exist, and this check reads that inventory rather than a second list. The rules hold per page, not per product: a product may render a page type as often as it needs, from as many files. Which page types are collections, and which of their slots are chrome rather than body, comes from `shells.collections`, Meridian's `{ collection: ["Heading", "Description"] }`.

The check reads code, not runtime state. A field shown only on a branch still counts, and both arms of one ternary count even if only one shows at a time. Menu-based filter facets are not questions. A page held in a variable and rendered as `{others}` is not seen as nested.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `content-page`: Legal: a third kind of page, help, which the config names under shells.content. It shows information and holds no primary action, so it is neither a primary-slot page nor a collection. It passes with "one job per page on 3 pages".
