## `check:inventories`

Inventory membership changes only by adopting a proposal, and each inventory's folders, barrels and uses match its list.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run check:inventories`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-inventories.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it. It compares the change with its base.

Flags:

- `--base <file>`: Compares with the product that config names in the working tree, instead of the pull request base. The fixtures have no history of their own, so this is how they test membership. The config itself is not compared then.
- `--proposals <dir>`: Needs `--base`. Reads that folder as the change's proposals.
- `--base-proposals <dir>`: Needs `--base`. Reads that folder as the base's proposals, matched with `--proposals` by file name.

It fails:

- A chrome layout, content layout or page type outside its allowlist, a directory under `paths.layouts`, `paths.contentLayouts` or `paths.pageTypes` with no list entry, or a list entry with no directory, and any other file directly in those directories besides `index.ts`.
- An import of a layout, content layout or page type under `paths.source` that is not on its list, a `pageTypes` export that does not match `allowed_page_types`, and a page-type barrel that re-exports an id not on it.
- A collection's ready body that is not one registered content layout, or that the feature passes ad-hoc children into, and a collection whose pages fill no slot outside its chrome, so no body is checked.
- The `shells` problems `check:one-thing` names, a page type in none or more than one of its three kinds, and a collection page type with no shell module or no shell, since the body check reads the same shells.
- Page CSS for a class the feature uses that no content layout, chrome layout or page type uses.
- A membership change against the base that no adopted proposal covers. A proposal covers a change when it is `status: decided` on the base, `status: adopted` in the change, and its `changes` on the base list, exactly, what changed: the member added or removed, the constant, the config field or its new value, each changed string in `flows` (a preview as `preview:<state>?<query>` or by its query alone, a bare one as `preview:<state>`; a state's first query drops its bare preview, so it is not an addition), `adapter.<field>` for an adapter field, the new adapter path, or the product's directory.
- A proposal the change adds, used to cover anything but what only adds or tightens. A change that only adds or only tightens passes with a proposal the change adds as `status: adopted`, with nothing under `changes`, `retires` or `opts-out`, that lists under `adds` each new member of the catalog exports, `allowed_layouts`, `allowed_content_layouts` or the flow states by its bare name, `page-type:<id>` for a new page type with its own new `shells` entry, `task:<id>` for a new task with its graph module and `preview:<state>?<query>` for a new preview pair, and under `tightens` `max_steps:<task id>` lowered, a cap lowered, `TARGET_MIN_PX` raised or `disclosed_sections:<section>` added. It covers nothing when it is on the base, when a base proposal already lists one of its `adds` for the same list, when one of its `adds` is a name the change removes or changes otherwise, or when one of its `tightens` loosens; nothing under `tightens` counts when the change moves any tightenable input the other way.
- A new page type whose change also alters a `shells` entry the base had, or that brings no entry of its own: that takes a decided proposal that lists the page type and the `shells` rules it touches under `changes`. A bare page type id under `adds` names nothing; it goes under `adds` as `page-type:<id>`.
- A base file with `export *` or `export =` that does not export a list by name, so a re-export cannot pass for a missing list.
- A config the base does not have at that path while the base has the product's inputs, so a renamed config needs a proposal.

Compared values: `allowed_layouts`, `allowed_content_layouts` and `disclosed_sections` once the base exports them; `allowed_page_types`; the catalog's export names; `modeledStates`; each task's `max_steps`; each priority item's action, rank and level; the caps and `TARGET_MIN_PX` in the rules module; every path in the config, its `flows` and `shells`; and the design system adapter, field by field, once the base config names one. Lists, tasks, `shells` entries, task graphs and previews are compared item by item, and string lists are sorted and de-duplicated first, so reordering is not a change. A new page type's pass line prints the `shells` rule and slots it joins. Names are compared, not values behind them, so pointing an existing name at another component is not a change.

A list the base does not export yet may be recorded once, without a proposal: `allowed_layouts`, `allowed_content_layouts` or `disclosed_sections`, and the design system adapter the config names. A base exports a list when it declares it with `export const` or names a local `const` in an export clause.

A product the base has neither the config nor the inputs of is moved or new. When git sees the inputs module renamed, the check compares with the base config whose `paths.inputs` named the old file, so a move shows as config path changes. A product with no such rename is new, a whole inventory added at once, which needs an adopted proposal that lists the product's directory.

Proposals are read from the config's `paths.proposals` folder, `proposals/` by default, at the base and in the change, matched by file name. [When a proposal is required](how-it-works.md#when-a-proposal-is-required) walks the rule, and [proposal 2026-11-12-right-size-governance](../../../proposals/2026-11-12-right-size-governance.md) records what takes one pull request. The approval is the code owner's merge: Ben, in this repository. Under `--base` a fixture compares no config, but a new page type still reads both configs' shells. A product cannot opt out of this rule.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `adds-a-page-type-with-its-shell`: Legal: the change adds the board page type with its own new entry under shells.collections, every entry the base had unchanged, and a proposal the change adds lists page-type:board under adds. A new page type with its own shells entry takes one pull request (proposal 2026-11-12-right-size-governance). It passes with "2026-11-12-board.md (only adds or tightens, so it is adopted in the pull request that adds it, which the code owner merges)".
- `adds-in-one-pull-request`: Legal: the inputs add the side-panel layout, and the proposal the change adds lists only side-panel under adds, already adopted. A proposal that only adds is adopted in the pull request that adds it. It passes with "0106-side-panel.md (only adds or tightens, so it is adopted in the pull request that adds it, which the code owner merges)".
- `content-page`: Legal: a third kind of page, help, which the config names under shells.content. It shows information and holds no primary action, so it is neither a primary-slot page nor a collection. It passes with "membership matches".
- `fake-ds`: Legal under the stand-in adapter, which shares no name with Todae. Run on the Todae adapter, every check here but the off-catalog lint fails these pages, so passing shows a check reads its names from the adapter. It passes with "collection bodies use a registered content layout".
- `page-type-in-two-pull-requests`: Legal: the change adds the board page type with its shells entry, and adopts a proposal decided on the base that lists board and shells.collections under changes. This is the second of the two pull requests a new page type takes. A fixture's base is not a git revision, so check:inventories does not compare shells here: the case proves the page type is covered, and the shells half rests on the same lists rule, compared on a real pull request base. It passes with "Adopts packages/harness/fixtures/page-type-in-two-pull-requests/proposals/2026-11-12-board.md".
- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "membership matches".
- `proposal-covers-change`: Legal: the inputs add the side-panel layout, and the change adopts a proposal that was decided on the base and lists side-panel under changes. It passes with "Adopts packages/harness/fixtures/proposal-covers-change/proposals/0102-side-panel.md".
- `re-exported-inputs`: Legal: the base exports allowed_layouts, allowed_content_layouts and disclosed_sections through export clauses, and the change keeps the same members as plain exports. It passes with "membership matches".
- `tightens-a-cap`: Legal: the change raises TARGET_MIN_PX from 24 to 32, a stricter rule input, and a proposal the change adds lists TARGET_MIN_PX under tightens, already adopted. A tightening takes one pull request. It passes with "TARGET_MIN_PX changed from 24 to 32. Adopts".
- `illegal/ad-hoc-content`: Illegal: a status board with page CSS as a collection's ready body, which is not a registered content layout. It fails with "not a registered content layout".
- `illegal/adds-a-page-type`: Illegal: the change adds the board page type with its shells entry, and a proposal the change adds lists board under adds by its bare name. A page type goes under adds as page-type:<id>, so the bare name covers nothing. It fails with "a proposal this change adds must list "page-type:board" under adds" and fails with "lists "board" under adds, but this change adds "page-type:board"".
- `illegal/adds-a-removal`: Illegal: the base has the side-panel layout and the change removes it, with a proposal the change adds that lists side-panel under adds. adds covers only members added, so a removal still needs a proposal decided on the base. It fails with "lists "side-panel" under adds, which this change removes or changes rather than adds".
- `illegal/adds-adopted-before`: Illegal: the inputs add the side-panel layout, and the only proposal that lists it under adds is already on the base. A proposal that only adds covers its members in the pull request that adds it, once, so it cannot let a later change through. It fails with "covered its change in an earlier pull request".
- `illegal/adds-alongside-a-rule-change`: Illegal: the change adds the side-panel layout and lowers TARGET_MIN_PX, with a proposal the change adds that lists both under adds. A proposal that names a change other than an addition is not one that only adds, so it covers neither. It fails with "lists "TARGET_MIN_PX" under adds, which this change removes or changes rather than adds, so it covers nothing".
- `illegal/adds-renamed-from-the-base`: Illegal: the inputs add the side-panel layout, and the proposal that lists it under adds is a proposal from the base under a new file name. A member a base proposal already lists under adds comes back only through a proposal decided on the base. It fails with "which a proposal on the base already lists under adds".
- `illegal/adds-rewrites-an-open-request`: Illegal: the inputs add the side-panel layout, and a request that is open on the base is rewritten in place as a proposal that only adds. A proposal on the base cannot become one that only adds: an open request is approved first. It fails with "is open on the base, so it cannot become a proposal that only adds".
- `illegal/adds-with-changes`: Illegal: the inputs add the side-panel layout, and the proposal the change adds lists side-panel under adds and TARGET_MIN_PX under changes. A proposal that adds in one pull request lists nothing else, so this one does not parse and covers nothing. It fails with "lists adds alongside changes".
- `illegal/adoption-not-marked`: Illegal: the proposal is decided on the base and lists side-panel, but the change does not mark it adopted, so it could cover the next change too. It fails with "Mark it "status: adopted" in this change".
- `illegal/adopts-open-request`: Illegal: the change adopts a proposal that is an open request on the base. Approval, open to decided, is its own pull request. It fails with "is an open request on the base".
- `illegal/adopts-with-its-proposal`: Illegal: the inputs add the side-panel layout, and the proposal that lists it is added in the same change. A proposal is adopted only after a designer has approved it on the base. It fails with "is added in this change".
- `illegal/body-slot-as-chrome`: Illegal: the config names the collection's Body slot as chrome, so no slot is left for the body rule to read. It fails with "CollectionPage pages fill no slot outside the chrome slots".
- `illegal/collection-without-body-slot`: Illegal: the config names every slot of the collection's shell as chrome, so its pages have no body slot, which a new collection entry would not show until it had pages. It fails with "so its pages have no body slot".
- `illegal/content-layout-expansion`: Illegal: the inputs add the board content layout, with its directory, and no proposal. The base is the fixture product. It fails with "without a proposal".
- `illegal/destructured-base-list`: Illegal: the base exports allowed_layouts through a destructuring declaration, which is not a list the check can read. It fails with "allowed_layouts is not a string array".
- `illegal/function-exported-base-list`: Illegal: the base exports allowed_layouts as a function, so the name is exported but is not a list the check can read. It fails with "allowed_layouts is not a string array".
- `illegal/inventory-expansion`: Illegal: the inputs add the side-panel layout, with its directory, and no proposal. The base is the fixture product. It fails with "without a proposal".
- `illegal/let-exported-base-list`: Illegal: the base exports allowed_layouts from a reassigned `let`, so the check cannot read the exported list from its initializer. It fails with "allowed_layouts is not a string array".
- `illegal/misspelled-chrome-slot`: Illegal: the config names the collection shell's chrome slot "Heding". CollectionPage has no such slot, so its Heading would be read as body. It fails with "names slot "Heding" for page type "collection", but CollectionPage has no such slot".
- `illegal/page-type-in-both-rules`: Illegal: the config names detail as a primary-slot page and a collection, which ask for one primary action and none. It fails with "page type "detail" in both primarySlots and collections".
- `illegal/page-type-in-primary-and-content`: Illegal: the config names detail as a primary-slot page and a content page, which ask for one primary action and none. It fails with "page type "detail" in both primarySlots and content".
- `illegal/page-type-moves-a-shell`: Illegal: the change adds the board page type with its own shells entry, and also changes the chrome slots of the collection entry the base had, with a proposal the change adds that lists page-type:board under adds. Only a new page type's own entry rides along with it, so neither is covered: changing an entry the base had takes a proposal decided on the base. It fails with "alters a shells entry the base had ("collection")".
- `illegal/proposal-for-another-adapter-change`: Illegal: the adapter makes "ghost" a primary variant, and the one adopted proposal is about a Toast. It names neither adapter.action nor the new adapter path. It fails with "a decided proposal must list "adapter.action"".
- `illegal/proposal-for-another-change`: Illegal: the inputs add the side-panel layout, and the one adopted proposal is about a catalog export. A proposal covers only the change it lists. It fails with "a decided proposal must list "side-panel" under changes".
- `illegal/proposal-names-path`: Illegal: the change adopts a decided proposal whose changes list `layouts/side-panel/`, a path, not the member side-panel. A proposal lists each name exactly. It fails with "a decided proposal must list "side-panel" under changes, and no adopted proposal lists".
- `illegal/re-exported-base-list`: Illegal: the base exports allowed_layouts as `export { layouts as allowed_layouts }`, and the change adds the side-panel layout with no proposal. It fails with "allowed_layouts changed from".
- `illegal/shell-rule-unknown-page-type`: Illegal: the shells rules name page types the product does not allow, so a rule would have no shell to read. It fails with "shells.collections names page type "wizard", which is not in allowed_page_types".
- `illegal/star-exported-base-inputs`: Illegal: the base inputs only `export * from` another module, so the check cannot tell whether the base exports allowed_layouts. It fails with "export *".
- `illegal/tightens-the-wrong-way`: Illegal: the change lowers TARGET_MIN_PX from 24 to 20, and a proposal the change adds lists TARGET_MIN_PX under tightens. A smaller touch target loosens the rule, so the proposal covers nothing. It fails with "lists "TARGET_MIN_PX" under tightens, but 24 to 20 loosens it, so it covers nothing".
- `illegal/tightens-with-changes`: Illegal: the change raises TARGET_MIN_PX, and the proposal the change adds lists it under tightens and MAX_VISIBLE_QUESTIONS under changes. A proposal that tightens in one pull request lists nothing else, so this one does not parse and covers nothing. It fails with "lists tightens alongside changes".
- `illegal/unclassified-page-type`: Illegal: the config names no collection, though the product has a collection page type, so the collection rules would read none of its pages. It fails with "page type "collection" in neither primarySlots nor collections".
- `illegal/undeclared-content-layout`: Illegal: a board content layout directory that allowed_content_layouts does not list. It fails with "undeclared content layout".
- `illegal/undeclared-layout`: Illegal: a side-panel layout directory that allowed_layouts does not list. It fails with "undeclared layout".

## `check:state-coverage`

Every modeled flow state has a view.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run check:state-coverage`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-state-coverage.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it.

It fails:

- A string in a flow's `modeledStates` that is not a `case` label in that flow's `views` module.
- A flow's states file that does not export `modeledStates`, or exports an empty list.

It matches strings, so it does not see whether the case renders anything distinct. Typecheck is a second gate for the same idea: `renderedStates` has to satisfy `ModeledState`.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "6 modeled states have views".
- `illegal/missing-view`: Illegal: invoice-approved is modeled and has no view. It fails with "has no view".

## `check:target-size`

Every control on every preview is at least 24 CSS px, or meets the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception, measured in headless Chrome.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run check:target-size`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-target-size.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it. It needs headless Chrome.

Flags:

- `--list`: Prints the previews it would open, without building or Chrome.

It fails:

- A control under 24 CSS px on a side that misses the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception, anywhere in the document: the page and the chrome around it, with each closed disclosure opened on its own.
- A button token floor under 24: the font size plus twice the vertical padding of the design system the adapter names.
- A `previews` entry for a state that is not modeled, or one that sets `state` itself, and a flow whose states file does not export `modeledStates` as a list of strings.
- A `paths.web` outside the repository or with no `index.html`, an app that does not build, and a built app that cannot be served.
- No Chrome found.

It builds the directory in `paths.web`, serves it with `vite preview` on a free port of 127.0.0.1, or uses the build `check:product` already serves for this product, and opens every state in each flow's `modeledStates` at 1280 by 900: bare, or once per query string that flow's `previews` in the config lists for it, such as `page=detail`. A state added later is opened without editing the script. A state that renders no `[data-page]` element is measured too. It clicks a disclosure summary on the page when one is present and measures, then opens every other closed disclosure in the document, such as a menu in the chrome, one at a time, measures what it shows, and closes it again.

It measures each preview on load and after a disclosure opens, at one width. The floor is `TARGET_MIN_PX` in the product's rules module. It closes the server and the browser itself.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "7 previews from modeledStates" (with --list) and passes with "controls on 7 previews meet 24 CSS px".
- `target-size-whole-document`: Legal: the page, the chrome around it, and a closed menu in the chrome have controls of at least 24 CSS px. check:target-size builds this folder's index.html. It passes with "controls on 7 previews meet 24 CSS px".
- `two-tasks`: Legal: a notes inbox with two tasks, each mapped to its own task graph, and a preview query for one modeled state only. It passes with "target size: preview ?state=archived" (with --list).
- `illegal/preview-sets-state`: Illegal: the preview query for "reminded" sets state=archived itself, so it would open another state than its key names. It fails with "sets state itself" (with --list).
- `illegal/small-control-in-closed-menu`: Illegal: two 12 CSS px links inside a closed menu in the chrome. The check opens every closed disclosure in the document on its own and measures what it shows. It fails with "a "Ready" is 12×12 CSS px and fails the spacing exception".
- `illegal/small-control-outside-page`: Illegal: two 12 CSS px links side by side in the chrome. They sit outside the [data-page] element, and the check measures the whole document. It fails with "a "Help" is 12×12 CSS px and fails the spacing exception".
- `illegal/stale-preview`: Illegal: a preview query for "confirming", which is not a modeled state, so it opens nothing. It fails with "previews names "confirming", which is not a modeled state" (with --list).

## `check:accessible-names`

On every preview, what a screen reader hears matches the flow's `accessible-names.ts`, and every press either announces what changed or moves focus.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run check:accessible-names`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-accessible-names.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it. It needs headless Chrome.

Flags:

- `--list`: Checks the file against the previews, without building or Chrome.

It fails:

- A control with no accessible name.
- An announcement the flow's `accessible-names.ts` declares for a preview that a screen reader does not hear there, compared by role, by name or text, and by every state the entry gives.
- A node the file leaves out whose announcement changes with the state: one with `aria-current`, which counts as declared only when its entry gives `current`; a live region, by role (`status`, `alert`, `log`, `timer`, `marquee`) or `aria-live` polite or assertive, with something to say; or a progress bar or meter.
- A missing file, a preview the file declares nothing for, or a key that is not a preview, with or without Chrome.
- A press that changes what a screen reader could read while no live region says anything new, focus stays put and the control's own expanded, checked, pressed or selected state stays the same.
- A press after which focus is on the page body, whatever was said.
- An action the check cannot focus, one that moves focus elsewhere when focused, and a preview that does not render the same actions on every load, so an action cannot be pressed on its own.
- An `accessible-names.ts` that does not load, a malformed `knownGaps` entry, and a `previews` entry that cannot be listed.
- A `knownGaps` entry whose press no longer has its problem on a preview it names, so the list only shrinks.
- A `knownGaps` entry with no `fixIn`, or one that is neither a GitHub issue or pull request URL nor the path of a proposal file that exists, with or without Chrome, so no gap waits on nothing.

It builds and serves the app as `check:target-size` does and opens the same previews. On each it reads the whole document's accessibility tree, the one a screen reader reads, through the DevTools protocol: each node's role, its accessible name, the text its subtree reads with `aria-hidden` runs left out, and `aria-current`, disabled, expanded, checked, pressed and selected. Chrome's tree does not carry `aria-current`, so it reads that from the element. Roles are Chrome's names, such as `image` and `DisclosureTriangle`. A node's text is its runs joined by a space, so write it the way a failure message prints it. Frames inside the page are not read.

Beside each flow's `views` module, `accessible-names.ts` exports `accessibleNames` (`satisfies AccessibleNames`): each preview mapped to what a screen reader should hear there. Declare what changes between states, not the whole tree. It reads each preview as it loads, so it does not open disclosures or wait for a live region to fill, and a state that should announce itself and renders no live region at all passes. [Proposal 2026-11-11-accessible-names-per-state](../../../proposals/2026-11-11-accessible-names-per-state.md) records the rule.

Then it presses every action. On each preview, from a fresh load with the origin's storage cleared, it focuses each enabled button, link, disclosure summary, menu item, tab, checkbox, radio or switch, checks that focus stayed on it, presses Enter, or Space for a checkbox, radio, switch, or checkbox or radio menu item, and reads the page 150 ms later, past the 100 ms Todae's announcer waits before it writes (inside an open Todae modal it writes later, which the check does not wait for). A new name on the focused control is not enough, and neither is a status region added with its words already in it, since screen readers do not reliably read either. A press that loads another document is skipped and not counted, and a dialog a press opens is dismissed.

Problems a product has not fixed yet go in the same file's `knownGaps` (`satisfies KnownGaps`), as `{ presses: ['button "Try again"'], problem: "focus lost", previews: ["state=error"], why, fixIn }`, where `fixIn` is the issue, pull request or proposal its fix waits on. Leaving `previews` out covers every preview, later ones included. A listed problem passes, and the check's last line counts them. [Proposal 2026-11-12-press-every-action](../../../proposals/2026-11-12-press-every-action.md) records the pass and what it cannot see, and [proposal 2026-11-12-shell-owned-focus](../../../proposals/2026-11-12-shell-owned-focus.md) adds `fixIn`.

Two patterns are fixed where every page shares them, so a page that uses them needs no listing, and the press check still catches one that does not: each product's shell moves focus to the new page's h1 on a page change, and a submit that turns itself off takes the catalog's `submitOff`, `aria-disabled` rather than `disabled`, so it keeps focus.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `announced-progress`: Legal: Meridian's invoice progress list as pull request 32 fixed it, built with Todae's Steps. After Approve, the current Payment stage reads "Next", as its declarations say. check:accessible-names builds this folder's index.html. It passes with "3 previews announce the 7 things their flows declare".
- `announced-sort`: Legal: a sort that says its new order through Todae's announcer, which writes its live region 100 ms after announce(). check:accessible-names reads each press after that, so the press is heard. It passes with "1 of 1 presses tell a screen reader what changed and keep focus on the page".
- `announced-waitlist`: Legal: Nook's Waitlist rows as pull request 42 fixed them. Each press keeps focus on the row's one button and says in the status region what changed. check:accessible-names presses every button on every preview. It passes with "6 of 6 presses tell a screen reader what changed and keep focus on the page".
- `listed-press-gap`: Legal: the silent leave from illegal/silent-waitlist-leave, listed in knownGaps while its fix waits for its own pull request. The check passes and counts it as known. It passes with "5 of 6 presses tell a screen reader what changed and keep focus on the page, and the other 1 has a problem its flow lists in knownGaps".
- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "7 previews declare 7 announcements" (with --list) and passes with "7 previews announce the 7 things their flows declare, and every control has a name. 9 of 9 presses".
- `illegal/no-declarations`: Illegal: the flow has no accessible-names.ts beside its views module. It fails with "accessible-names.ts is missing. Beside the flow's views module" (with --list).
- `illegal/silent-waitlist-leave`: Illegal: Nook's Waitlist from pull request 42 after its first fix and before its second. Leaving Birch's waitlist while Cedar is free turns the row's button into Join waitlist, keeps focus on it, and leaves the status region as it was, so a screen reader hears nothing. It fails with "pressing button "Leave waitlist for Birch" changes the page, and a screen reader hears nothing".
- `illegal/stale-declaration`: Illegal: the declarations name a preview the flow does not open, so they would compare nothing there. It fails with ""state=ready" is not a preview of this flow" (with --list).
- `illegal/stale-press-gap`: Illegal: knownGaps still lists the silent leave after the fix that says it, on announced-waitlist's page. A gap that no longer happens fails, so the list only shrinks. It fails with "knownGaps lists button "Leave waitlist for Birch" as "silent", and pressing it on ?state=freed no longer has that problem".
- `illegal/step-read-as-in-progress`: Illegal: pull request 32's bug. After Approve, Todae's Steps reads the waiting Payment stage as "In progress: Payment due Nov 18, 2026", and the declarations say it is next. It fails with "expects listitem reading "Next: Payment due Nov 18, 2026" (aria-current="step"), and a screen reader does not hear it. Its listitem nodes are "Done: Received", "Done: Approval", "In progress: Payment due Nov 18, 2026" (aria-current="step")".
- `illegal/undeclared-current-step`: Illegal: pull request 32's list with declarations that leave it out. The current step's announcement changes with the state, so the check asks for it to be declared, and the declaration puts "In progress: Payment due" in front of the reviewer. It fails with "listitem reading "In progress: Payment due Nov 18, 2026" (aria-current="step") changes with the state, and".
- `illegal/undeclared-preview`: Illegal: the declarations leave out one preview, changes-requested, so nothing says what a screen reader hears there. It fails with "declares nothing for "state=changes-requested"" (with --list).
- `illegal/unnamed-control`: Illegal: an icon-only button with no label. Every declaration holds, and a screen reader still announces the button as only "button". It fails with "button <button type="button" class="more-actions"> has no accessible name".
- `illegal/untracked-press-gap`: Illegal: knownGaps lists the silent leave from listed-press-gap without fixIn, so nothing tracks its fix. Every gap names the issue, pull request or proposal its fix waits on. It fails with "knownGaps[0] needs fixIn: where its fix is tracked" (with --list).
- `illegal/waitlist-row-loses-focus`: Illegal: Nook's Waitlist rows from pull request 42 before its fix. Joining swaps the row's Join waitlist button for a new Leave waitlist button, and focus falls to the page body. The status region says the right thing, and the check still fails. It fails with "pressing button "Join waitlist for Cedar" removes it from the page, and focus falls to the page body".

## `check:rendered-page`

Every preview, as Chrome paints it at desktop and phone width: section headings two type-scale steps below the title, the rank-1 action in the first view, disclosures closed unless the state opens them, AA contrast in light and dark, and no sideways scroll on a phone.

A rule check: `check:rules` runs it, and `check:product` runs it on each product. Run it as `npm run check:rendered-page`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-rendered-page.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it. It needs headless Chrome.

It fails:

- A heading on a page, a disclosure summary included, that sits fewer than two steps below the page's title on the design system's type scale, or fewer than one step when it is inside an item of a list or table that holds two items or more. The title is the first visible h1, or `role="heading"` at level 1, in each `[data-page]` element. Measured at 1280 by 900 and 390 by 844.
- A page with no visible title, and a preview with no `[data-page]` element.
- On a page type with a primary slot, a rank-1 action from `priority` that is not whole inside the first view, or whose centre something else covers, at 1280 by 900 or 390 by 844, before any scroll; and such a page that shows no rank-1 action at all.
- A disclosure, a `<details>` whose summary a person can see, or one with no summary, that is open on load at either width, unless the flow's `accessible-names.ts` declares it with `expanded: true` on that preview.
- A run of text under WCAG AA contrast, 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text, against the background colours of its element and its ancestors, in the light or the dark colour scheme, anywhere in the document; and a page where every run of text sits over a background image or gradient, so none can be measured.
- At 390 by 844, a page wider than the box it lays out in: the document, the `[data-page]` element or any of its ancestors, so the page scrolls sideways or an app shell cuts it off. The message names the first elements past the edge.
- At 390 by 844, a page that lays out wider than the phone because its `index.html` has no viewport meta.
- A design system stylesheet with no type scale: no family of at least three tokens named `--<prefix>font-size-<n>`, and a page on which fewer than three of them have a size.
- A `previews` entry that cannot be listed, a `paths.web` that does not build or serve, and no Chrome found, as `check:target-size` fails them.

It builds and serves the app as `check:target-size` does, or uses the build `check:product` serves, and opens the same previews three times: at 1280 by 900 in the light colour scheme, at 1280 by 900 in the dark one, and at 390 by 844 as a phone, light. It reads each as it loads and presses nothing. Every rule is a pattern that holds on any page: no number is set per page or per page type, and the steps, the views and the AA ratios are the harness's, not a product input. [Proposal 2026-11-12-rendered-page](../../../proposals/2026-11-12-rendered-page.md) records the rule.

The type scale is the numbered font-size tokens in the stylesheet the adapter names: Todae's `--todae-font-size-1` to `-6`, 12 to 30 px. The names come from the stylesheet, and Chrome computes each size on the page in each view, so a size set with `clamp()`, `calc()` or a media query counts as painted; a page that does not load the stylesheet falls back to the sizes it writes. A design system whose sizes are not numbered this way has no scale here, and needs an adapter field, which is a proposal. A size counts as the step at or below it, and a size within half a pixel of a step counts as that step. With Todae's 30 px title, section headings are 20 px or smaller and record names in a list 24 px or smaller. A list or table of one item is a section, not a list of records. Only size counts, so a heading set apart by weight or colour alone passes.

The rank-1 action is found by its name, from `aria-labelledby`, `aria-label` or its text, as the `action` of each `priority` item at rank 1, among the page's buttons and links. One copy whole in view with nothing over its centre, through any open shadow root, passes, so a pinned action row passes by design. Content and collection pages hold no primary, so they are not measured.

Contrast reads every text node a person can see, the chrome's included, against the background colours of its element and its ancestors, down to the first opaque one, faded by their opacity, over the canvas Chrome paints for the root's colour scheme or its `color-scheme` meta. It does not sample pixels, so text placed over something that is not its ancestor, such as a badge positioned over a photo, is read against its ancestors. Text over a background image or gradient is skipped and counted in the last line. Text in a control that is turned off is exempt, as WCAG allows. It emulates `prefers-color-scheme`, so a product whose tokens follow the system scheme is read in both; one that switches with an attribute, a class or a stored setting is read in light twice. A field's own value and placeholder are not text nodes, so they are not read.

A disclosure's name is its summary's `aria-label` or text, which is what it is matched by against `accessible-names.ts`. A box inside the page that scrolls sideways on purpose, such as a wide table's wrapper, is not measured for phone width.

It sees only what each preview shows as it loads: a state a press reveals, data no preview renders, and a long page with correct hierarchy pass. The critique of the screenshots judges those.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "7 previews at 1280 by 900 and 390 by 844: section headings sit 2 type-scale steps below the title (list items 1), "Approve" is in the first view in".
- `rendered-page-patterns`: Legal: record names one step below the title inside a list, a disclosure the state opens and declares expanded, a menu whose summary is hidden, an action row pinned under a long page, visually hidden text, a turned-off button's faint text, and text over a gradient, which is skipped and counted. It passes with "disclosures load closed (1 opened by their state)" and passes with "(1 over an image, not measured)".
- `illegal/cut-off-in-an-app-shell`: Illegal: the shell clips the document to the view, so the document never grows, but the page inside it is 640 px wide on a 390 px phone and scrolls sideways in its pane. It fails with "at 390 by 844: the page is wider than main, which it lays out in: 640 CSS px in 390, so it scrolls sideways or is cut off. Past the edge: div.line-items".
- `illegal/dark-scheme-contrast`: Illegal: the text follows the dark scheme and the page's white ground does not, as Nook's did on main before its ground took the canvas token. Light passes; dark fails. It fails with "dark colour scheme: text under WCAG AA contrast: "Northwind Office Supply" is #eeeeee on #ffffff".
- `illegal/disclosure-open-on-load`: Illegal: Line items loads open, and no accessible-names.ts declares it expanded, so no state opens it. It fails with "the disclosure "Line items" is open on load".
- `illegal/heading-in-a-one-item-list`: Illegal: a list of one item is a section in disguise, so its heading sits two steps under the title like any section heading. It fails with "section heading h2 "Vendor" is 24px, 1 type-scale step below the title".
- `illegal/no-phone-viewport`: Illegal: with no viewport meta, Chrome lays a phone page out about 980 px wide and shrinks it to fit. It fails with "px wide on a 390 px phone, so everything on it is shrunk. Add <meta name="viewport"".
- `illegal/page-without-a-title`: Illegal: the page's name is bold text, not an h1, so the check has no title to hold its headings to, and a screen reader has none to land on. It fails with "detail page: no visible title".
- `illegal/primary-below-the-fold`: Illegal: Approve, the rank-1 action, sits under 1000 px of content, below the first view at desktop and phone width, as PR 49's was before it pinned its action row. It fails with "at 1280 by 900: "Approve" is at" and fails with "at 390 by 844: "Approve" is at".
- `illegal/primary-covered`: Illegal: Approve sits in the first view, but a fixed banner lies over it, so a person cannot reach it without dismissing something first. It fails with "but div.cookie-banner "We use cookies." covers its centre".
- `illegal/section-heading-near-title`: Illegal: a 24 px section heading under a 30 px title, one step of Todae's type scale. Sections sit at least two steps below the title, as PR 48 and PR 49's Later today, Amenities, Vendor and Activity did not. It fails with "section heading h2 "Vendor" is 24px, 1 type-scale step below the title".
- `illegal/sideways-scroll-on-a-phone`: Illegal: a 640 px block fits a desktop view and pushes the page past a 390 px phone's edge. It fails with "at 390 by 844: the page scrolls sideways, 640 CSS px wide in a 390 px view. Past the edge: div.line-items".

## `check:opt-outs`

Every opt-out in a product's config stands on an adopted proposal that names the rule and the product.

A product check: it reads one product's config, and is not one of `check:rules`. Run it as `npm run check:opt-outs`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-opt-outs.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it.

It fails:

- An entry in the config's `optOuts` that names a rule `check:rules` does not run, or a core rule, `lint:product-ui` or `check:inventories`.
- An opt-out whose proposal is missing, is not directly in `paths.proposals` (`proposals/` by default), is not `status: adopted`, or has no `opts-out` entry naming the rule and the product's `paths.source`, as `<rule> for <paths.source>`.

`check:product` runs it before any rule check, so a rule is skipped only on an opt-out that passed here. [Proposal 0008](../../../proposals/0008-rule-opt-out-and-retirement.md) and [proposal 0011](../../../proposals/0011-proposal-fields-and-graduation.md) have the rules.

Fixture cases, under `packages/harness/fixtures/`, that run it:

- `opt-out`: Legal: the fixture product opts out of check:disclosure on an adopted proposal that names the rule and the product. It passes with "opts out of check:disclosure, each on an adopted proposal".
- `product`: Legal: the fixture product as it is. Every check passes it, so a case fails for what it changes, and npm run new:product starts a product from a copy that passes. It passes with "has no opt-outs, so every harness rule applies".
- `illegal/opt-out-core-rule`: Illegal: an opt-out of check:inventories, a core rule, even on an adopted proposal that names it. It fails with "cannot be opted out".
- `illegal/opt-out-missing-proposal`: Illegal: an opt-out that names a proposal file that is not there. It fails with "does not exist".
- `illegal/opt-out-open-proposal`: Illegal: an opt-out whose proposal is an open request, not an adopted decision. It fails with "is open, not adopted".
- `illegal/opt-out-other-product`: Illegal: an opt-out that borrows a proposal written for another product. It fails with "does not opt out check:disclosure for".
- `illegal/opt-out-outside-proposals`: Illegal: an opt-out whose proposal sits outside the config's proposals directory, where CODEOWNERS does not ask for review. It fails with "is not a proposal file directly in".
- `illegal/opt-out-unknown-rule`: Illegal: an opt-out of a rule check:rules does not run. It fails with "is not a rule in check:rules".

## `check:products`

Runs `check:product` on every product the registry finds, one after another, so a new product needs no script or CI job of its own.

A repository check: it reads the repository, not one product. Run it as `npm run check:products`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-products.ts`. It takes no `--config`. It needs headless Chrome.

Flags:

- `--json`: Prints the product configs as a JSON array and runs nothing. CI reads it to give each product its own job.

It fails:

- Any product whose `check:product` run fails. It runs the rest first, then names every product that failed.
- No product: no `harness.config.ts` outside the harness package.
- An argument other than `--json`.

A product is any `harness.config.ts` git knows of, tracked or new and not ignored, outside `packages/harness/` (`lib/products.ts`), and still in the working tree. Nothing lists products by hand: `check:proposals`, `check:retirement`, `check:trace` and CI read the same registry.

## `check:proposals`

Every proposal has its fields and sections, a new one has a dated name, and each status moves one step at a time from the base.

A repository check: it reads the repository, not one product. Run it as `npm run check:proposals`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-proposals.ts`. It takes no `--config`. It compares the change with its base.

It fails:

- A proposal without front matter, with an unknown or missing `status` (`open`, `decided` or `adopted`) or `changes`, or a field that is not a list.
- `adds` or `tightens` beside `changes`, `retires` or `opts-out`, or on a proposal that is not `adopted`, and an `opts-out` entry that is not `<rule> for <paths.source>`.
- An empty or missing `## Reason`, `## Preview` or `## Adoption`, and the names before the rename, `status: graduated` and `## Graduation`, which only a base proposal may still have.
- A `## States` section that misses an edge case (Empty, Loading, Error, Long content, Permissions, Over time), gives a state no text, marks one `Out of scope` without a reason, lists only edge cases, or puts `None` beside other states.
- Compared with the base: a status that moves more than one step or backwards; a change to a decided or adopted proposal's `changes`, `retires`, `opts-out`, `adds` or `tightens`; a decided or adopted proposal renamed or deleted.
- Compared with the base: a new proposal that starts `adopted` while it lists anything under `changes`, `retires` or `opts-out`.
- Compared with the base: a proposal that lists anything under `changes` or `adds` with no `## States` when it is new or moves from `open` to `decided`, and a decided or adopted proposal that drops the `## States` it had.
- A proposal the change adds or renames whose file name is not a real date no later than tomorrow in UTC and a lowercase slug, such as `2026-11-12-side-panel.md`, or that shares its name with a proposal in another proposal folder.

It reads `proposals/`, each product config's `paths.proposals`, and every other folder named `proposals` that git knows of outside the harness package, so a proposal seeded for a later `paths.proposals` move is checked when it lands. A proposal is a file ending in `.md`, in that case, other than `README.md`; a `.MD` file is not read.

It takes no `--config`. Proposals already on the base keep their text, without `## States`, until they move to `decided`. The proposals that merged with a number, from 0001, keep those names. `proposals/README.md` has the format, and the Vitest suite in `packages/harness/src/lib/proposals.test.ts` proves the rules, since the check reads the repository's own folders.

## `check:retirement`

A rule most products opt out of is flagged for retirement, and a rule leaves `check:rules`, or a product opts out, only by adopting a proposal.

A repository check: it reads the repository, not one product. Run it as `npm run check:retirement`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-retirement.ts`. It takes no `--config`. It compares the change with its base.

It fails:

- Two configs that name the same `paths.source`.
- Any product's opt-outs that fail the rules of `check:opt-outs`, so a product no `check:<name>` script runs cannot carry one either.
- A rule a majority of products, and at least two, opt out of. With two products, both must.
- Compared with the base: a rule that leaves `check:rules` unless an adopted proposal lists it under `retires`, and a new opt-out unless its proposal is adopted in the change and listed it under `opts-out` when it was decided.

A product is any `harness.config.ts` git knows of, tracked or new, outside the harness package, whose fixtures are not products. A tracked config deleted from the working tree is no longer a product. A rule is identified by its script name. [Proposal 0008](../../../proposals/0008-rule-opt-out-and-retirement.md) has the rule, and `packages/harness/src/lib/opt-outs.test.ts` tests the threshold.

## `check:loop`

The design loop graph in `packages/harness/design-loop.ts` is one an agent can follow, and the diagram in `how-it-works.md` is the one it draws.

A repository check: it reads the repository, not one product. Run it as `npm run check:loop`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-loop.ts`. It takes no `--config`.

Flags:

- `--write`: Redraws the diagram in `docs/how-it-works.md` from the graph.

It fails:

- A dangling edge or an unreachable node.
- An eval node that names a script `package.json` lacks, or has no retry on `fail`.
- A human gate with no `CODEOWNERS` owner.
- An end the run can reach without an eval node passing after the last change.
- A diagram in `packages/harness/docs/how-it-works.md` that is not the one the graph draws.

The loop is the harness's, and every product follows the same one. [Proposal 0009](../../../proposals/0009-design-loop-graph.md) records the graph, and `packages/harness/src/lib/loop.test.ts` tests it.

## `check:docs`

The check reference and the docs that copy it are the ones the code writes: `npm run docs:gen` rewrites them.

A repository check: it reads the repository, not one product. Run it as `npm run check:docs`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-docs.ts`. It takes no `--config`.

Flags:

- `--write`: Rewrites the stale docs. `npm run docs:gen` runs it with this flag.

It fails:

- `packages/harness/docs/checks.md`, or a generated block in the harness README, `CLAUDE.md` or the verify skill, that is not what the code writes now.
- A doc missing a block's `<!-- docs:gen <block> start -->` or `end` marker, or holding either twice.
- An npm script that runs a harness file with no `<file>.meta.ts` beside it, or a meta no script runs.
- A meta that is not a tool and lists nothing it fails, or a rule check whose meta says it is a tool.
- A `.meta.ts` that does not export `meta`, a script that imports a relative file that is not there, and a `case.ts` that is not plain literals.
- A meta that names a fixture case `illegal/<name>` or an `npm run <script>` that does not exist, and a fixture case that runs a script that is not a harness script.

Each harness script's meta, `packages/harness/src/<file>.meta.ts`, typed `satisfies CheckMeta`, gives the words: a summary, the flags it reads, what it fails, and how it works. Everything else is read from the code: script names and the build gate from `package.json`, rule checks from `check:rules`, `--config` from whether the script loads `lib/config.ts`, the base from whether it calls `resolveBaseRev`, Chrome from whether it loads `puppeteer-core`, and fixture cases from each `case.ts` and its doc comment. For a script that loads `lib/config.ts`, the config loader accepts only the flags its meta lists, so a documented flag is a read one.

So a pull request that adds or changes a check updates its meta and runs `npm run docs:gen`, which keeps `CLAUDE.md` and the verify skill current with it.

## `check:fixtures`

The harness's own tests: every illegal fixture case fails with its expected message, and every legal case passes with its.

A repository check: it reads the repository, not one product. Run it as `npm run check:fixtures`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-fixtures.ts`. It takes no `--config`.

It fails:

- An illegal case whose check passes, or fails without the phrase its `case.ts` expects; a legal case whose check fails, or passes without its phrase.
- A case folder with no `case.ts`, a `case.ts` that names a path that does not exist or a script that is not one harness check, or an expected phrase that is part of a path the case names, since a crash prints the path.
- A case name given on the command line that is no case folder.
- A `case.ts` with an unknown key, no checks, a check that gives both or neither of `fails` and `passes`, `args` that set `--config`, `--base`, `--proposals` or `--base-proposals`, or proposals with no base to compare with.

`packages/harness/fixtures/product/` is a small product with its own `harness.config.ts` that every check passes. Every other folder directly under `fixtures/` or `fixtures/illegal/` is a case whose `case.ts`, plain literals, changes some of that config's paths and names the checks to run on the result, each as its npm script with `--config`, with the phrase each must print. A case that sets `base` may also give `proposals` and `baseProposals`, folders `check:inventories` reads as the change's proposals and the base's, matched by file name. The stand-in design system in `fixtures/fake-ds/` shows a check reads its names from the adapter, and small products of their own show a rule reads its product's config and inputs.

Name cases to run only those: `npm run check:fixtures -- illegal/two-primaries`. The cases that run a Chrome check without `--list` open a page, so they need Chrome as the check does; the build gate section above names the Chrome lookup.

## `check:product`

Runs `check:opt-outs`, then every rule check in `check:rules`, on one product, skipping a rule the product opts out of.

A product check: it reads one product's config, and is not one of `check:rules`. Run it as `npm run check:product`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-product.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it. It needs headless Chrome.

It fails:

- No `--config <file>`, or any other argument beside it.
- The first check that fails on that product. It stops there.
- An app in `paths.web` that does not build or serve, when a check that opens it is next.

It reads the rule checks from `check:rules` in `package.json`, in its order, so the two cannot drift, and says which rules it skips. Typecheck, ESLint and the Vitest suite read the whole repository, so `npm run check` runs them once and `check:products` runs this once per product.

The checks that open the app in Chrome, `check:target-size` and `check:accessible-names`, share one build of it: just before the first of them it builds `paths.web` and serves it with `vite preview` on a free port, then hands each the address. Run on its own, either check builds and serves its own copy the same way.

## `check:trace`

A change that touches a product carries a loop trace, and every trace it adds or edits is a walk the design loop graph allows.

A repository check: it reads the repository, not one product. Run it as `npm run check:trace`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/check-trace.ts`. It takes no `--config`. It compares the change with its base.

It fails:

- A change that touches a product's directory, the folder of any `harness.config.ts` outside the harness package, and adds or edits no trace under `traces/`.
- A trace the change adds or edits that does not start at the graph's `start`, steps between nodes no edge connects, gives a router, eval or human step no `when` or one its edges lack, or stops anywhere but a checkpoint.
- A trace that ends its run with a change to checked state that no passing eval node follows. A run paused at a checkpoint with an edge out may stop unchecked.
- A file under `traces/` that is not a `.jsonl` trace or the folder's README.
- A trace line that is not a JSON object, has a key other than `node`, `when` and `at`, has a value that is not a string, has no `node`, or names a node the design loop does not have.

It is not in `npm run check`, because the eval node runs the gate in the middle of the walk, before the trace ends at a checkpoint. CI runs it after the build gate, and an agent runs it before pushing. `npm run loop:step` writes a trace step by step. A trace is the agent's own record, so passing shows the record is a walk the graph allows, not that the work was done: [proposal 0010](../../../proposals/0010-loop-trace.md). Only traces the change adds or edits are read.

## `critique`

The design loop's `critique` step: writes the brief for a second model to judge the screenshots, then records its findings and the edge back to build or on to the note.

A tool: the build gate does not run it. Run it as `npm run critique`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/critique.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it.

Flags:

- `--gallery <dir>`: The screenshots folder `npm run screenshots` wrote, `products/<name>/review/screenshots/<change>`, in the `--config` product's own `review/screenshots`.
- `--brief <file>`: Writes the critic's brief there. Keep it out of the repository, such as in a scratch folder.
- `--findings <file>`: The critic's answer, one JSON object. It is checked against the gallery, written into it as `CRITIQUE.md`, and the edge to take is printed with the block for the pull request description.
- `--trace <file>`: Goes with `--findings`: the change's trace, `traces/<change>.jsonl`. It must be a walk the graph allows whose last step is `screenshots`, and its `critique` steps that took `revise` count the rounds so far.

The harness calls no model. Run `npm run critique -- --config <product config> --gallery <dir> --brief <file>` and give the brief it writes to a model other than the one that built the change, with the screenshots it names. The brief gives the product's tasks and ranked actions and a rubric of four patterns that hold on any page: hierarchy, the primary action, grouping and crowding. The critic judges relationships and weight, never counts. Each finding names its pattern, `revise` or `note`, the `after` screenshots it shows in, the problem and the fix.

With `--findings` and `--trace`, a finding that calls for `revise` sends the loop back to `build`, until two rounds have: the third critique of a run prints `pass`, and what is left open goes in the review note with the `note` findings. A retake of the screenshots replaces the folder, `CRITIQUE.md` included, so the next round's critique is of the new screenshots. It is advisory: the build gate does not run it, and no check reads `CRITIQUE.md`. [Proposal 2026-11-12-critique-step](../../../proposals/2026-11-12-critique-step.md) records it.

## `loop:step`

Appends one step to a change's loop trace, and refuses a step the design loop graph does not allow.

A tool: the build gate does not run it. Run it as `npm run loop:step`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/loop-step.ts`. It takes no `--config`.

Run it as `npm run loop:step -- traces/<change>.jsonl <node> [when]`, with the `when` of the edge taken out of a router, eval or human node. It writes only a `.jsonl` file under `traces/`, so a wrong edge shows up at the step that takes it, not at `check:trace`. `traces/README.md` has the format.

## `new:product`

Starts a product: copies the harness's fixture product, which passes every check, to `products/<name>/` and points its config there.

A tool: the build gate does not run it. Run it as `npm run new:product`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/new-product.ts`. It takes no `--config`.

Run it as `npm run new:product -- <name>`, with a lowercase slug. It refuses a folder that already exists. The registry finds the new product from its config, so `npm run check` and CI check it with nothing else to edit. A new product is a whole inventory added at once, so `check:inventories` passes it only with an adopted proposal that lists `products/<name>` under `changes`, decided on the base. The copy is the fixture's invoice approval: rename and reshape it from there, one proposal at a time.

## `screenshots`

The design loop's `screenshots` step: captures each preview before and after a change into a gallery the pull request links.

A tool: the build gate does not run it. Run it as `npm run screenshots`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/screenshots.ts`. It needs `--config <file>`, a product's `harness.config.ts`, and reads every path from it. It needs headless Chrome.

Flags:

- `--out <dir>`: The gallery folder, `products/<name>/review/screenshots/<change>`. Each run replaces it whole, with the `CRITIQUE.md` the `critique` step wrote of the old screenshots.
- `--state <state>`: Keeps the previews of that state. Repeat it for each state the change touches, or leave it out for every preview.
- `--base <ref>`: Also captures the previews at that commit, so the folder holds `before/` and `after/`.
- `--pin <dir>`: Takes only `--config`. Points each image's link in a committed gallery at the raw PNG at that commit, and prints the line for the pull request description. It refuses a folder with anything but its `README.md` uncommitted.

It opens the previews `check:target-size` opens, at 1280 by 900 in the same Chrome, from the app `check:product` serves for this product or one it builds and serves on a free port, and writes `before/` and `after/` PNGs and a gallery `README.md` whose images each link to their own file. Commit the folder, run `--pin`, commit the `README.md` again, and put the line `--pin` prints in the pull request description with `<sha>` replaced by the pushed commit's full SHA, with its whole `https://github.com/` address: a relative path breaks in the GitHub app and in email, and a branch link breaks once the branch is deleted. Images in the description itself don't come through from an agent. [Proposal 2026-11-11-screenshot-gallery](../../../proposals/2026-11-11-screenshot-gallery.md) records it.

## `setup:chrome`

Installs the chrome-headless-shell build `puppeteer-core` pins into `.cache/chrome`, where the Chrome checks look for it.

A tool: the build gate does not run it. Run it as `npm run setup:chrome`, from the repository root, defined in `packages/harness/src/setup-chrome.ts`. It takes no `--config`.

CI runs it too, so a local run measures in the same build. Nothing is installed system-wide.
